headline: Record profit as volume and pricing outpace fuel costs
summary_short: Union Pacific posted record Q2 2026 net income of $1,993M (+6.2% y/y) and diluted EPS of $3.36 (+6.7% y/y) as revenue rose 11.5% to $6,864M on volume growth, pricing gains, and higher fuel surcharge, even as the operating ratio rose 70bp y/y to 59.7%.
summary_long: Revenue rose 12% y/y to $6,864M on higher fuel surcharge, volume growth (carloads +2%), pricing gains, and other revenue, partly offset by mix; freight revenue ex-fuel grew 4%. Fuel cost jumped 63% on higher per-gallon price, lifting the operating ratio 70bp y/y to 59.7% (adjusted 59.2%, +110bp). Operating income rose 9% to $2,763M; net income rose 6% to $1,993M ($3.36 diluted EPS, +7%; adjusted EPS $3.41, +13%). YTD free cash flow was $1,812M; cash rose to $1,614M from $1,266M at year-end. Management raised full-year EPS growth guidance to high-single-digit and reaffirmed operating-ratio-improvement and capital-allocation guidance.
